writer.model: inherited native agent; API does not provide exact version

production_gate.publication_authority: Owner authorization is handled by parent; this draft grants no approval.

research_method: Institutional source pages were opened before drafting. Evidence and limits are author mapping, not an independent factual verdict. Two pages from one institution count as one institution.

episodes.title_en: Why Does a Breeze Dry Clothes Faster?
episodes.title_zh: 微風吹，衣服為何乾得比較快？
episodes.question: Why can moving air speed up drying?
episodes.description_en: A breeze carries water vapor away from wet fabric. Compare matching cloths while keeping temperature and humidity the same.
episodes.description_zh: 微風會帶走濕布旁的水蒸氣。固定溫度、濕度與布料，看看空氣流動如何加快乾燥。

sources.title: Evaporation Loss During Sprinkler Irrigation
sources.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Wind is an important factor', extracted lines 27–29.
sources.evidence: Wind transports water vapor away and replaces moist air near an evaporating surface.
sources.limits: Agricultural context; transfer principle applies to a wet surface, but its loss percentages are not used for clothes.

sources.title: Evaporation and Climate
sources.locator: Opening clothesline example and paragraph 'Wind speed', extracted lines 3–7.
sources.evidence: Wind carries water vapor away; dry, windy conditions increase evaporation.
sources.limits: Avoid the page's informal language that air 'holds' water and its oversimplified temperature-energy explanation.

sources.title: Humidity, Evaporation, and Boiling
sources.locator: Humidity and evaporation discussion, extracted lines 32–41.
sources.evidence: Evaporation occurs below boiling; water-vapor partial pressure affects net evaporation.
sources.limits: Molecular inset is symbolic; no humidity or drying-time prediction.

sources.title: What's the difference between evaporation and boiling?
sources.locator: Factors affecting evaporation, extracted lines 56–68: wind, humidity and surface evaporation without bubbles.
sources.evidence: Moving air and lower humidity can increase evaporation. Evaporation occurs at the surface and does not require boiling.
sources.limits: Educational explanation, not measured clothing drying times.

claims.text: Moving air can increase evaporation by carrying vapor away from a wet surface, replacing the moist air nearby.
limits: Compare equal initial water, fabric, exposed area, temperature and ambient humidity; do not promise faster drying in every weather condition.

claims.text: Liquid water can become water vapor below boiling; humidity influences the net rate.
limits: Vapor is individual molecules, not visible miniature liquid droplets. No air water-capacity container metaphor.

invariants: Two cloths begin with equal water content, material and exposed area. Same room temperature and ambient humidity; only nearby airflow differs.
At the same microscopic viewing scale, every water symbol has the same size in liquid and vapor. Track departures; no shrinking molecules.
Vapor markers remain distinct from broad airflow arrows. No steam cloud, boiling bubbles or visible droplet spray.
The contrast is qualitative and time-compressed, not a measured two-times drying rate.
episodes.simplification: An isothermal schematic of mass transfer. Real airflow can also change cloth temperature; that coupled effect and sunlight are excluded.

diagram_scale.cloth_panels: Two equal 300 by 380 px cloth rectangles at x=170 and x=610; no numerical fabric size asserted.
diagram_scale.molecular_inset: 12 equal-radius water markers initially on each matched patch; departures are tracked in the surrounding air region.
diagram_scale.time: Use 'Time compressed' during the wet-area comparison.

cues.en: Two equally wet shirts. Why can the one in a breeze dry faster?
cues.zh: 兩件一樣濕的衣服，為什麼吹到微風的那件可能乾得更快？
cues.visual: Illustrated clothesline; match shirts, then reveal a breeze beside the right shirt.

shot_plan.action: Illustrated clothesline; match shirts, then reveal a breeze beside the right shirt.
shot_plan.controls: Equal fabric, water and exposed area; breeze is the only comparison change.

cues.en: First, water can evaporate from wet cloth without ever reaching its boiling point.
cues.zh: 先看濕布：水不用沸騰，也能從布上蒸發。
cues.visual: Magnify one damp fiber patch into a separate symbolic molecular inset.

shot_plan.action: Magnify one damp fiber patch into a separate symbolic molecular inset.
shot_plan.controls: Keep actual shirt scene separate from inset; no bubbles or steam.

cues.en: Water molecules leave the surface and become invisible water vapor in the air.
cues.zh: 水分子離開表面，變成空氣中看不見的水蒸氣。
cues.visual: A few equal-sized water markers leave the wet patch; explain that visible markers are symbols.

shot_plan.action: A few equal-sized water markers leave the wet patch; explain that visible markers are symbols.
shot_plan.controls: Same marker radius across phases. No liquid-drop trail drawn as vapor.

cues.en: In still air, moisture builds up near the fabric, slowing further net evaporation.
cues.zh: 空氣不流動時，布旁的水蒸氣會增加，讓淨蒸發變慢。
cues.visual: Show vapor markers returning as well as leaving in the still-air panel.

shot_plan.action: Show vapor markers returning as well as leaving in the still-air panel.
shot_plan.controls: Some exchange continues; do not freeze all molecular motion or declare zero evaporation.

cues.en: A breeze carries that vapor away and brings less humid air alongside the cloth.
cues.zh: 微風把附近的水蒸氣帶走，讓較乾的空氣來到布旁。
cues.visual: Flow arrows carry vapor markers sideways out of the near-surface region.

shot_plan.action: Flow arrows carry vapor markers sideways out of the near-surface region.
shot_plan.controls: Ambient air is less humid than the moist boundary layer; do not change room humidity between panels.

cues.en: That lets more water escape overall, so the wet patch can shrink faster.
cues.zh: 整體離開的水就能更多，濕的部分也可能縮小得更快。
cues.visual: Resume equal-time cloth panels; reduce wet-area tint faster on the breezy side.

shot_plan.action: Resume equal-time cloth panels; reduce wet-area tint faster on the breezy side.
shot_plan.controls: Tint shows remaining wet area, not changing molecule size; qualitative rates only.

cues.en: Keep temperature, starting wetness, and fabric the same for a fair comparison.
cues.zh: 比較時，要固定溫度、起始含水量，以及布料。
cues.visual: Brief checklist connects both shirts with matching badges.
cues.overlay_en: Same temperature | Same fabric | Same water

shot_plan.action: Brief checklist connects both shirts with matching badges.
shot_plan.controls: No sun or heater appears on just one side.

cues.en: The breeze helps by removing nearby vapor. It does not make water disappear.
cues.zh: 微風的幫助，是帶走附近的水蒸氣；水並沒有消失。
cues.visual: Return to clothesline and follow a final vapor symbol beyond the shirt.

shot_plan.action: Return to clothesline and follow a final vapor symbol beyond the shirt.
shot_plan.controls: No vanishing molecule effect; markers leave the crop through a visible outflow.

episodes.title_en: What Holds a Suction Cup Down?
episodes.question: Why is a sealed suction cup hard to lift?
episodes.description_en: A suction cup seals a region of lower air pressure. The higher pressure outside helps keep it against a smooth surface.
episodes.description_zh: 吸盤封住一小塊氣壓較低的空間；外側較高的氣壓，幫忙把它壓在平滑表面上。

sources.title: Demos: 2A-01 Suction Cups
sources.locator: Description and explanation, extracted lines 103–107.
sources.evidence: A cup on a smooth surface resists removal; lifting the rim admits air. The pressure difference accounts for the holding force.
sources.limits: The complete-vacuum force estimate is an ideal upper bound and is deliberately excluded.

sources.title: Balloon and Cup Attraction
sources.locator: Explanation, extracted lines 23–27; tip around line 58.
sources.evidence: Expelling air and increasing the sealed volume reduces inside pressure; greater outside pressure holds the cup.
sources.limits: Balloon-and-cup demonstration differs from a rubber suction cup; only the pressure-difference mechanism is transferred.

claims.text: When a cup seals a region of lower air pressure, the greater outside pressure produces a net push toward the surface; admitting air reduces the difference.
limits: Use a flexible cup and a smooth nonporous horizontal surface. The cavity still contains air; no perfect vacuum or universal holding load.

invariants: Use the same cup on horizontal glass throughout, avoiding unspoken friction needed for a hanging vertical load.
Show some air remaining under the cup; never label the cavity a perfect vacuum.
Pressure acts from all directions; diagram selected opposing vertical contributions only, labelled 'Pressure forces: simplified'.
Lifting the edge creates an actual open route for air before the inside/outside labels equalize; the seal is not magnetic or glue.
episodes.simplification: Selected pressure forces and elastic cup recovery are shown qualitatively. Seal leakage and rubber stiffness affect real performance.

diagram_scale.cup: One 440 px wide cup on a horizontal glass strip y=1180; cross-section is a separate inset.
diagram_scale.pressure: Paired broad force arrows toward/away from glass with qualitative labels; no 1-atmosphere cavity assumption.
diagram_scale.release: Lift a 45 px rim segment; draw incoming air through that visible gap.

cues.en: This cup is hard to lift off smooth glass. What is holding it down?
cues.zh: 吸盤貼上平滑玻璃後，很難直接提起。是什麼把它壓住？
cues.visual: A hand gently tugs a cup straight upward from horizontal glass; it stays sealed.

shot_plan.action: A hand gently tugs a cup straight upward from horizontal glass; it stays sealed.
shot_plan.controls: No vertical wall or unsupported heavy object.

cues.en: Pressing the flexible cup flattens it and pushes some air out around the rim.
cues.zh: 壓下柔軟的吸盤，吸盤變扁，部分空氣從邊緣跑出去。
cues.visual: Cross-section flattens; a few air markers exit before the rim seals.

shot_plan.action: Cross-section flattens; a few air markers exit before the rim seals.
shot_plan.controls: Show outward path while rim is open; not all air removed.

cues.en: The rim seals against the glass as the cup tries to spring back.
cues.zh: 邊緣貼住玻璃形成密封，吸盤則試著恢復原來的形狀。
cues.visual: Rim contacts glass; dome recovers slightly with trapped air still visible.

shot_plan.action: Rim contacts glass; dome recovers slightly with trapped air still visible.
shot_plan.controls: Cup recovery increases cavity volume without lifting the sealed edge.

cues.en: The trapped air now has lower pressure than the air outside the cup.
cues.zh: 裡面剩下的空氣，氣壓就比吸盤外面低。
cues.visual: Reveal a lower-pressure label in the cavity and higher-pressure label outside.
cues.overlay_en: Inside: lower pressure | Outside: higher pressure

shot_plan.action: Reveal a lower-pressure label in the cavity and higher-pressure label outside.
shot_plan.controls: Residual particles remain inside; no 'vacuum' label.

cues.en: That pressure difference gives a net push toward the glass, helping hold the cup.
cues.zh: 這個氣壓差形成朝向玻璃的淨推力，幫忙把吸盤壓住。
cues.visual: Selected opposing pressure arrows combine into a downward net-arrow inset.

shot_plan.action: Selected opposing pressure arrows combine into a downward net-arrow inset.
shot_plan.controls: Arrows are schematic integrated pressure forces, not individual air jets.

cues.en: Now lift just one edge. Air can flow through the new opening underneath.
cues.zh: 只要掀起一個邊角，空氣就能從開口進入吸盤下面。
cues.visual: Lift the rim tab; inward markers pass through the new opening.

shot_plan.action: Lift the rim tab; inward markers pass through the new opening.
shot_plan.controls: Do not equalize before a visible opening exists.

cues.en: The pressures become more nearly equal, and the cup comes away much more easily.
cues.zh: 內外氣壓變得比較接近，吸盤就容易拿下來了。
cues.visual: Pressure labels converge, net arrow fades, then cup lifts clear.

shot_plan.action: Pressure labels converge, net arrow fades, then cup lifts clear.
shot_plan.controls: Release is continuous; do not depict a magic sudden disappearance of all air.

cues.en: A good seal preserves the pressure difference. Suction is a push from outside.
cues.zh: 好的密封能維持氣壓差；吸盤的作用，來自外面較大的推力。
cues.visual: Return to the intact cup and briefly replay the outside-pressure arrow.

shot_plan.action: Return to the intact cup and briefly replay the outside-pressure arrow.
shot_plan.controls: Qualify with higher outside pressure; no claim of an inward pulling vacuum force.

episodes.title_en: Why Does a Sliding Book Stop?
episodes.title_zh: 滑出去的書，為什麼會停下？
episodes.question: What slows a book sliding across a level table?
episodes.description_en: After your hand lets go, kinetic friction opposes the book's slide. Its motion energy is transferred mainly into thermal energy.
episodes.description_zh: 手放開後，動摩擦力阻礙書本滑動；書本的運動能量，主要轉成書本與桌面的熱能。

sources.title: Kinetic Friction
sources.locator: Kinetic friction section, extracted lines 144–170, especially sliding right / friction left example.
sources.evidence: Kinetic friction opposes relative sliding; an unpushed sliding object slows and stops.
sources.limits: The simple constant-coefficient model is approximate; static friction at rest need not be nonzero.

sources.title: Nonconservative Forces
sources.locator: Opening discussion and Example 7.9, extracted lines 23–25 and 67–81.
sources.evidence: Friction reduces mechanical energy; sliding-to-rest example relates work to lost kinetic energy and thermal energy.
sources.limits: No claim that total energy disappears or that all friction is dissipative.

sources.title: Physics 2211 Quiz 3 Solutions, Spring 2021
sources.locator: PDF page index 4 (printed page 5), question 5, extracted lines 219–238.
sources.evidence: For a book sliding on a table, the book-plus-table system gains thermal energy from kinetic friction.
sources.limits: Its worked example has a hand maintaining speed; use it for energy transfer only, not as the unforced deceleration demonstration.

claims.text: After the hand releases a book sliding on a horizontal table, kinetic friction opposes the slide and slows it.
limits: No continuing horizontal hand force. Air drag is neglected. Clamp motion at rest rather than reverse it.

claims.text: During the slide, mechanical energy is transferred mainly into thermal energy of the book and table.
limits: Some energy can also become sound and deformation. Temperature rise may be too small to feel; no glow or sparks.

invariants: Keep hand visibly clear after release; weight and table normal balance vertically.
Rightward velocity and leftward kinetic-friction arrows coexist during sliding; after rest, remove the kinetic-friction arrow and never reverse the book.
Total-energy accounting retains the initial energy; use thermal-energy increase in book plus table, not a disappearing energy bar.
Do not generalize to ideal rolling without slipping or say all static friction necessarily dissipates energy.
episodes.simplification: A level, stationary table with approximately constant kinetic friction; sound and deformation are minor unquantified channels.

diagram_scale.book: 240 by 95 px book sliding right across a 900 px table.
diagram_scale.optional_internal_model: If numeric motion is needed, m=1 kg, v0=2 m/s, mu_k=0.2, g=9.8 m/s^2; t_stop≈1.02 s and x_stop≈1.02 m. This is a model, not measured footage.
diagram_scale.motion: Scale 600 px/m for that optional model; slowed playback must say 'Slow motion'. Qualitative nonnumeric animation is also allowed.

cues.en: Give a book a shove. Once your hand lets go, why does it stop?
cues.zh: 推一下桌上的書。手放開後，它為什麼會停下來？
cues.visual: A hand pushes a book right, then lifts completely clear as the book slides.

shot_plan.action: A hand pushes a book right, then lifts completely clear as the book slides.
shot_plan.controls: Table is horizontal and stationary.

cues.en: The book is sliding across the table, and the two surfaces rub together.
cues.zh: 書本在桌面上滑動，兩個接觸的表面彼此摩擦。
cues.visual: Enlarge the contact region into a schematic rubbing-surface inset.

shot_plan.action: Enlarge the contact region into a schematic rubbing-surface inset.
shot_plan.controls: Do not present giant interlocking teeth as a literal universal microscopic mechanism.

cues.en: Kinetic friction acts opposite the slide: here, the book moves right, friction points left.
cues.zh: 動摩擦力的方向，和滑動相反：書往右滑，摩擦力就向左。
cues.visual: Blue velocity arrow points right; orange friction-force arrow points left.

shot_plan.action: Blue velocity arrow points right; orange friction-force arrow points left.
shot_plan.controls: Different colors and labels distinguish velocity from force.

cues.en: With no hand still pushing, that opposing force makes the book slow down.
cues.zh: 沒有手繼續推，這個反向的力就讓書本逐漸減速。
cues.visual: Equal-time position markers become closer together as the book slows.

shot_plan.action: Equal-time position markers become closer together as the book slows.
shot_plan.controls: Speed decreases continuously; no camera movement disguising speed.

cues.en: Its energy of motion has not vanished. Much becomes thermal energy in both surfaces.
cues.zh: 運動的能量沒有消失；大部分轉成書本和桌面的熱能。
cues.visual: Motion-energy bar falls while book-plus-table thermal-energy increment rises.

shot_plan.action: Motion-energy bar falls while book-plus-table thermal-energy increment rises.
shot_plan.controls: Bars balance within the stated simplified model; no new energy from nothing.

cues.en: Energy spreads through the book and table; the diagram exaggerates it for clarity.
cues.zh: 能量散布在書本和桌面中；圖解為了看清楚，做了誇張呈現。
cues.visual: Small distributed thermal markers highlight both contact regions, with no visible glow.

shot_plan.action: Small distributed thermal markers highlight both contact regions, with no visible glow.
shot_plan.controls: No red-hot book, smoke, numerical temperature claim or claim of a measured experiment.

cues.en: When the book stops sliding, this kinetic-friction arrow stops too; it does not reverse.
cues.zh: 書本停止滑動後，這支動摩擦力箭頭也收起；書不會因此倒滑。
cues.visual: Book rests; velocity and kinetic-friction arrows fade to zero.

shot_plan.action: Book rests; velocity and kinetic-friction arrows fade to zero.
shot_plan.controls: No other horizontal force is present, so no static-friction arrow is needed.

cues.en: Friction transfers energy and changes the book's motion. The total energy has not disappeared.
cues.zh: 摩擦把能量轉移出去，改變書本的運動；總能量並沒有消失。
cues.visual: Return to the resting book with the completed energy-transfer diagram.

shot_plan.action: Return to the resting book with the completed energy-transfer diagram.
shot_plan.controls: Conservation refers to the book-plus-table-plus-surroundings system, not the book's kinetic energy alone.

episodes.title_en: Why Do Bridges Have Expansion Gaps?
episodes.title_zh: 橋上的伸縮縫，有什麼用？
episodes.question: Why can a bridge need a gap between sections?
episodes.description_en: Bridge materials generally expand when they warm. An expansion joint leaves room for movement rather than forcing the deck to buckle.
episodes.description_zh: 橋梁材料受熱通常會膨脹。伸縮縫預留移動空間，減少橋面受限制時產生的熱應力。

sources.title: Thermal Expansion
sources.locator: Figure 1.5 expansion joints and linear thermal expansion section; extracted lines 34–49.
sources.evidence: Most materials expand when heated over ordinary ranges; bridge joints allow length changes without buckling.
sources.limits: Thermal expansion coefficients vary by material and temperature; not every material always expands.

sources.title: 770.7 Maintenance of Bridge Superstructure
sources.locator: Section 770.7.7 Expansion Joint Maintenance, extracted lines 96–100.
sources.evidence: Expansion joints accommodate bridge movement caused by temperature changes.
sources.limits: Real joints also accommodate other movements and have many designs; no engineering design prescription is given.

claims.text: Temperature changes make ordinary bridge materials change length; an expansion joint accommodates the resulting movement.
limits: Use an ordinary temperature range and one schematic span fixed at one end and free to move at the other. Not all bridges require the same visible joint.

invariants: Keep the pier positions fixed; show one deck end on a sliding bearing and the other end fixed, with a gap against the next fixed reference section.
Warmer deck becomes longer and the shown gap becomes narrower. Cooler deck becomes shorter and the gap widens.
The gap remains open in the normal illustration; do not teach that normal joints must slam shut in hot weather.
Thermal expansion displacement is exaggerated and labelled; no material identity, actual joint dimension or temperature-derived numerical promise is implied.
episodes.simplification: One-dimensional expansion of one span, ignoring temperature gradients, structural loads, creep and multi-span details.

diagram_scale.span: Deck from x=130 to x=740 when cool; adjacent fixed reference begins x=870. Draw fixed bearing left and sliding bearing right.
diagram_scale.comparison: Warm deck endpoint x=790, same adjacent reference x=870. 50 px movement is exaggerated, not a real bridge measurement.
diagram_scale.labels: Fixed end | Sliding bearing | Expansion gap | Movement exaggerated

cues.en: This gap in a bridge is deliberate. Why leave space in a solid road?
cues.zh: 橋面上的這道縫是刻意留下的。好好的路，為什麼要留空間？
cues.visual: Illustrated car passes over a covered bridge joint; reveal a simple side-view inset.

shot_plan.action: Illustrated car passes over a covered bridge joint; reveal a simple side-view inset.
shot_plan.controls: Road joint cover remains plausible; do not show a wheel-trapping hole.

cues.en: Most bridge materials expand when they warm up and contract when they cool down.
cues.zh: 多數橋梁材料變熱時會膨脹，變冷時則會收縮。
cues.visual: Side-view span changes from cool blue tint to warm orange tint.

shot_plan.action: Side-view span changes from cool blue tint to warm orange tint.
shot_plan.controls: Tint indicates temperature only, not melting or material transformation.

cues.en: Across a long span, even a small fractional change can mean noticeable movement.
cues.zh: 橋跨很長，即使只增加一小部分長度，也可能產生明顯位移。
cues.visual: Reveal a long span and enlarge its moving endpoint with a linked inset.

shot_plan.action: Reveal a long span and enlarge its moving endpoint with a linked inset.
shot_plan.controls: No invented numerical movement; magnification inset is explicitly separate.

cues.en: An expansion joint provides room for the bridge deck to change its length.
cues.zh: 伸縮縫就是預留空間，讓橋面能夠改變長度。
cues.visual: Label gap and sliding bearing; fixed piers remain still.

shot_plan.action: Label gap and sliding bearing; fixed piers remain still.
shot_plan.controls: One end fixed, one sliding; do not stretch fixed supports.

cues.en: In this simplified view, the warming deck lengthens and the gap becomes narrower.
cues.zh: 在這個簡化圖中，橋面變熱伸長，旁邊的縫就變窄。
cues.visual: Animate warm deck endpoint toward adjacent reference while gap shrinks.

shot_plan.action: Animate warm deck endpoint toward adjacent reference while gap shrinks.
shot_plan.controls: Left fixed end and adjacent reference do not move; never scale the whole image.

cues.en: As the deck cools and shortens, that same gap becomes wider again.
cues.zh: 橋面冷卻縮短時，同一道縫又會變寬。
cues.visual: Reverse the endpoint displacement and restore the cool view.

shot_plan.action: Reverse the endpoint displacement and restore the cool view.
shot_plan.controls: Changes use the same bridge and viewing scale.

cues.en: Blocking thermal movement can create large stresses, so engineers design ways to accommodate it.
cues.zh: 熱脹冷縮的移動若受到阻擋，就可能產生很大的應力，因此工程上要預留移動方式。
cues.visual: Briefly compare free movement with a restrained schematic carrying a stress label.

shot_plan.action: Briefly compare free movement with a restrained schematic carrying a stress label.
shot_plan.controls: No sensational bridge collapse; frame as design purpose, not a prediction for this bridge.

cues.en: The gap is useful space: it lets the bridge respond to changing temperature.
cues.zh: 這道縫是有用的空間，讓橋梁能隨溫度變化調整長度。
cues.visual: Return to the original bridge and highlight the joint unobtrusively.

shot_plan.action: Return to the original bridge and highlight the joint unobtrusively.
shot_plan.controls: Do not imply every bridge uses this exact joint or that temperature is the only load.

episodes.title_en: Why Does Tightening a String Raise Its Pitch?
episodes.title_zh: 琴弦拉緊，音調為什麼升高？
episodes.question: How does tension change the pitch of the same guitar string?
episodes.description_en: With vibrating length held fixed, increasing string tension increases its vibration frequency and raises pitch.
episodes.description_zh: 固定同一根琴弦的有效振動長度，提高張力會使振動頻率增加，音調也會升高。

sources.title: Strings, standing waves and harmonics
sources.locator: Tension and tuning discussion, extracted lines 90–98, especially line 91 and the frequency formula.
sources.evidence: Increasing tension raises frequency; the fundamental depends on length, tension and linear mass density.
sources.limits: Ideal flexible string model. Real tightening slightly stretches the string; use a modest tuning change.

sources.title: The rule of strings and pitch
sources.locator: Pitch factors at extracted lines 8–14.
sources.evidence: Tightening raises pitch; thickness and vibrating length also affect pitch. Nut and saddle support the sounding string length.
sources.limits: Instrument-maker educational source, independent of UNSW; not a claim that length or thickness never changes in real tuning.

claims.text: For the same string with essentially fixed vibrating length and linear density, greater tension produces a higher vibration frequency and pitch.
limits: Compare one open string, with no fretting or string replacement. Modest tuning approximates fixed linear density. Pluck amplitude is not the pitch control.

invariants: One open string between fixed nut and saddle throughout. No fretting, thicker replacement string or changing visible active length.
Both comparison strings show the fundamental: one spatial half-wave and two fixed endpoint nodes. More temporal oscillations, not more spatial loops, represent higher fundamental frequency.
Use the same pluck displacement and viewing scale so loudness is not substituted for pitch.
When showing tension arrows, they point outward at opposite endpoints. String transverse motion is perpendicular to its resting length.
The moving waveform is explicitly slow motion and its cycles are not literal audio-rate motion.
episodes.simplification: Ideal fundamental-mode string with fixed active length and approximately fixed mass per unit length. Real strings have harmonics and stiffness; no exact pitch ratio is promised.

diagram_scale.string: Horizontal active length x=160..920, baseline y=850; endpoint nodes fixed.
diagram_scale.animation: Use y(x,t)=A*sin(pi*(x-160)/760)*cos(phase(t)), A=55 px for both conditions; tighter-string phase advances faster while both retain one half-wave.
diagram_scale.comparison: Compare 2 versus 3 schematic cycles in an equal visual time window, labelled 'Slow motion'; these are visual rates, not claimed measured notes.

cues.en: Turn this guitar's tuning peg, tighten one string, and its note rises. Why?
cues.zh: 轉動吉他的調音鈕，把一根弦拉緊，音調就升高。為什麼？
cues.visual: Same illustrated guitar and open string; hand turns its tuning peg.

shot_plan.action: Same illustrated guitar and open string; hand turns its tuning peg.
shot_plan.controls: No fret pressed; string identity does not change.

cues.en: Keep the same string and the same vibrating length between its two supports.
cues.zh: 先固定同一根弦，以及兩個支點之間的有效振動長度。
cues.visual: Reveal nut and saddle with a fixed length bracket.

shot_plan.action: Reveal nut and saddle with a fixed length bracket.
shot_plan.controls: Active-length bracket remains constant.

cues.en: Turning the peg increases the tension: the string is pulled more strongly along its length.
cues.zh: 調音鈕增加張力，也就是把弦沿著長度方向拉得更緊。
cues.visual: Isolate the active string; outward endpoint arrows increase in length.

shot_plan.action: Isolate the active string; outward endpoint arrows increase in length.
shot_plan.controls: Tension arrows lie along the resting string, not vertically.

cues.en: When plucked, the tighter string completes more vibrations in the same amount of time.
cues.zh: 撥動後，較緊的弦在相同時間內，能完成更多次振動。
cues.visual: Two equal-duration slow-motion insets show lower- and higher-tension fundamentals.

shot_plan.action: Two equal-duration slow-motion insets show lower- and higher-tension fundamentals.
shot_plan.controls: Higher temporal frequency; same one-half-wave mode and same amplitude.

cues.en: More vibrations per second means a higher frequency, which we hear as higher pitch.
cues.zh: 每秒振動次數更多，就是頻率較高；聽起來，音調也比較高。
cues.visual: Cycle counters advance faster on the tighter string; return to guitar.

shot_plan.action: Cycle counters advance faster on the tighter string; return to guitar.
shot_plan.controls: Counters are schematic; no claim of a real measured note.

cues.en: The drawing is slowed down. Real musical strings vibrate far too quickly to follow.
cues.zh: 這是放慢的示意圖；真正演奏時，琴弦振動得快得多。
cues.visual: Expose a clear slow-motion badge and one fixed-end waveform.

shot_plan.action: Expose a clear slow-motion badge and one fixed-end waveform.
shot_plan.controls: Do not imply the drawn 2–3 cycles per visual second are guitar audio frequency.

cues.en: Here, both plucks start with the same displacement, so tension is the control we change.
cues.zh: 這裡兩次撥弦的起始位移相同，因此比較時只改變張力。
cues.visual: Keep equal pluck-size markers while highlighting only the tension control.

shot_plan.action: Keep equal pluck-size markers while highlighting only the tension control.
shot_plan.controls: Avoid the absolute claim that amplitude has no possible effect on real-string frequency.

cues.en: Same string, same length, greater tension: faster vibration, and a higher note.
cues.zh: 同一根弦、相同長度，張力更大，就振動更快、音調更高。
cues.visual: End on the unchanged guitar with tension and frequency badges.

shot_plan.action: End on the unchanged guitar with tension and frequency badges.
shot_plan.controls: No broken string or unsafe extreme tightening; modest tuning only.

episodes.title_en: Why Do Small, Timed Pushes Build a Swing?
episodes.title_zh: 小小推一下，鞦韆為什麼越盪越高？
episodes.question: Why do pushes timed with a swing's natural rhythm work well?
episodes.description_en: A helper can add energy by pushing in step with a swing's motion. Timing matters; resistance still removes energy.
episodes.description_zh: 配合鞦韆的自然節奏推，可以有效加入能量；推的時機很重要，阻力也仍持續帶走能量。

sources.title: Forced Oscillations and Resonance
sources.locator: Driving, damping and child-on-swing example; extracted lines 30–45, especially line 45.
sources.evidence: A parent driving a child on a swing near its natural frequency transfers energy effectively; damping reduces response.
sources.limits: Small-amplitude oscillator analogy. Do not reuse the page's oversimplified Tacoma Narrows explanation.

sources.publisher: Appalachian State University Department of Physics and Astronomy
sources.title: A driven mass on spring
sources.locator: Demonstration explanation around extracted line 36.
sources.evidence: Correctly timed repeated input, illustrated by pushing a child on a swing, builds motion near the system's natural frequency.
sources.limits: The demonstration apparatus is a mass on a spring. Apply the swing analogy qualitatively, not its measured frequency.

claims.text: A helper who pushes in step with a swing's natural rhythm can add energy repeatedly and build its amplitude; damping removes energy.
limits: External helper pushes, not a rider pumping by changing body geometry. Moderate amplitudes; no unlimited growth or exact fixed period at large angles.

invariants: Keep pivot, rope length, rider mass and camera fixed; rider does not actively change body geometry.
A helper push appears only in a brief interval as the seat passes the low point moving away from the helper; tangential force points along velocity in that interval.
Remove the hand/force arrow on the return path. Do not automatically push in one direction through both halves of a cycle.
Raise peak angle gradually, roughly 10 to 25 degrees, without lengthening ropes or moving the pivot.
Depict energy as added by the helper, with ongoing losses, not created by resonance. Keep the peak finite.
episodes.simplification: Moderate-angle externally driven pendulum. The approximate natural rhythm is useful here; the exact period varies with large amplitude, and real helper pushes are not sinusoidal.

diagram_scale.angle_range: Start at ±10 degrees; build to at most ±25 degrees. Geometry must keep seat distance from pivot constant.
diagram_scale.timing: One short push per full back-and-forth cycle, near the bottom on the outward pass. Motion is schematic; avoid a claimed real period.
diagram_scale.force: For theta measured from downward vertical, use seat=(xp+L*sin(theta), yp+L*cos(theta)); force tangent in the sign of theta_dot during the push.

cues.en: A few small pushes can make a swing climb higher. Why does timing matter?
cues.zh: 小小推幾次，就能讓鞦韆盪得更高。為什麼時機這麼重要？
cues.visual: Helper beside a small-amplitude swing; show successive modest peaks.

shot_plan.action: Helper beside a small-amplitude swing; show successive modest peaks.
shot_plan.controls: Same rope length, pivot and rider throughout.

cues.en: A swing has a natural back-and-forth rhythm: one complete cycle returns to its starting point.
cues.zh: 鞦韆有自然的來回節奏；一個完整循環，會回到原來的狀態。
cues.visual: Let the swing coast briefly; a subtle cycle marker follows one complete return.

shot_plan.action: Let the swing coast briefly; a subtle cycle marker follows one complete return.
shot_plan.controls: One complete cycle means the same position and direction, not merely crossing the same point.

cues.en: A helper pushes as the rider moves away, adding energy in the motion's direction.
cues.zh: 幫忙的人在乘坐者往前離開時推，沿著移動方向加入能量。
cues.visual: Short tangential force arrow appears near the low point on the away pass.

shot_plan.action: Short tangential force arrow appears near the low point on the away pass.
shot_plan.controls: Hand force aligns with velocity only during brief contact; label it as force.

cues.en: Wait for the next cycle, then add another push at the matching moment.
cues.zh: 等下一次循環，再在相配的時機補上一推。
cues.visual: Helper waits while seat returns, then repeats at the same phase.

shot_plan.action: Helper waits while seat returns, then repeats at the same phase.
shot_plan.controls: No push on the returning seat or continuous horizontal force.

cues.en: Those repeated, well-timed inputs can build a larger motion from individually small pushes.
cues.zh: 一次次配合節奏加入能量，單次小推也能累積成較大的擺動。
cues.visual: Show peak-angle markers growing gradually from 10 to 25 degrees.

shot_plan.action: Show peak-angle markers growing gradually from 10 to 25 degrees.
shot_plan.controls: Amplitude growth requires energy input; rope never stretches to create height.

cues.en: Driving near the natural rhythm is called resonance: energy transfer becomes especially effective.
cues.zh: 以接近自然節奏驅動，就是共振；能量傳遞會特別有效。
cues.visual: Link the repeating helper push to the cycle marker.

shot_plan.action: Link the repeating helper push to the cycle marker.
shot_plan.controls: Qualitative weakly damped oscillator explanation; no exact resonance formula claimed.

cues.en: Air resistance and friction still remove energy, so the growth cannot continue without limit.
cues.zh: 空氣阻力和摩擦仍會帶走能量，因此擺幅不會無限制地增加。
cues.visual: Two small loss arrows balance later inputs; peak-angle markers stop growing.

shot_plan.action: Two small loss arrows balance later inputs; peak-angle markers stop growing.
shot_plan.controls: No energy recycling loop or zero-loss real swing.

cues.en: To build the swing, add energy at the right time, cycle after cycle.
cues.zh: 要讓鞦韆盪高，就在正確時機，一輪又一輪地加入能量。
cues.visual: Return to a comfortable finite swing and one correctly timed push.
cues.overlay_en: The right push, at the right time

shot_plan.action: Return to a comfortable finite swing and one correctly timed push.
shot_plan.controls: This is a model explanation, not a dangerous swing-height challenge.

episodes.title_en: Why Do You Lean Forward When a Car Brakes?
episodes.title_zh: 車一煞車，人為什麼往前傾？
episodes.question: Why does a passenger tend to move forward relative to a braking car?
episodes.description_en: The car slows, while your body tends to keep its motion. A backward force from the restraint helps slow you with the car.
episodes.description_zh: 車開始減速時，身體傾向維持原來的運動；安全帶等約束提供向後的力，讓人也跟著減速。

sources.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
sources.locator: First-law statement, extracted lines 18–20.
sources.evidence: Without a net external force, an object maintains straight-line constant-velocity motion.
sources.limits: General law, not a vehicle crash test or injury-reduction statistic.

sources.title: Newton's First Law of Motion: Inertia
sources.locator: First law and friction discussion, extracted lines 30–35.
sources.evidence: A net force is required to change velocity; inertia is resistance to a change of motion.
sources.limits: Use an approximately inertial ground frame; do not introduce a forward pseudo-force.

sources.title: The Law of Inertia: Newton's First Law
sources.locator: Description paragraph, extracted line 260.
sources.evidence: The video description explicitly identifies a seatbelt as an external force stopping a pilot.
sources.limits: Read the page description, not the linked full video. NASA Glenn and NASA STEM together are one institution, not two.

claims.text: As a car slows, the passenger's body tends to retain its motion; changing its velocity requires a net external force.
limits: Explain in a stationary ground frame. The passenger's relative forward movement does not require a new forward force.

claims.text: A restraint can exert a backward force that slows the passenger with the vehicle.
limits: The car illustration applies the first law and the NASA restraint example; forces also arise from the seat and other contacts. No crash performance or medical claim.

invariants: Show a belted illustrated passenger from the start. Do not propose an unbelted real demonstration.

Car and passenger initially move right together relative to fixed ground markers. Car slows; the passenger can briefly move forward relative to the car while still moving forward relative to the ground.
Use blue rightward velocity arrows and orange backward force arrows with distinct labels. Never draw a forward arrow labelled 'Inertia force' in the ground frame.
The belt remains anchored to the car and exerts a backward force on the torso during slowing; it is not a forward pushing jet.
Do not show the car instantly stop while the restrained passenger travels metres unopposed. Use modest relative lean and overlapping deceleration.
episodes.simplification: A schematic straight-line braking interval with a belted passenger. Body flexibility, belt stretch, seat forces and braking dynamics are not quantified.

diagram_scale.car: Side cutaway occupying x=100..980, y=700..1280, facing right. Fixed ground tick marks establish the frame.
diagram_scale.motion: Torso leans forward by about 35 px relative to the seat while both remain moving right and decelerating; this pixel shift is illustrative.
diagram_scale.vectors: Velocity and force use separate color/legend. Only velocity-arrow lengths encode speed, never acceleration or pressure.

cues.en: The car brakes, and you lean forward. Did something suddenly push you that way?
cues.zh: 車一煞車，你就往前傾。是突然有什麼把你往前推嗎？
cues.visual: Side-view cutaway of a belted passenger leaning slightly forward during braking.

shot_plan.action: Side-view cutaway of a belted passenger leaning slightly forward during braking.
shot_plan.controls: Illustration only; no real unsafe braking demonstration.

cues.en: Before braking, you and the car are moving together at the same speed.
cues.zh: 煞車之前，你和車子一起移動，速度相同。
cues.visual: Fixed ground ticks pass beneath car and passenger; equal blue velocity arrows appear.

shot_plan.action: Fixed ground ticks pass beneath car and passenger; equal blue velocity arrows appear.
shot_plan.controls: Use the ground frame and straight, level road.

cues.en: Braking slows the car, but your body tends to keep its previous motion.
cues.zh: 車子煞車減速時，身體卻傾向維持原來的運動。
cues.visual: Car velocity arrow shortens; torso begins a small forward lean relative to seat.

shot_plan.action: Car velocity arrow shortens; torso begins a small forward lean relative to seat.
shot_plan.controls: Body slowing can overlap car slowing; do not show a completely force-free belted interval.

cues.en: That tendency is inertia. Changing your body's velocity requires a net external force.
cues.zh: 這個傾向叫作慣性。要改變身體的速度，需要外力的合力。
cues.visual: Freeze with a simple first-law badge; no new forward force arrow.

shot_plan.action: Freeze with a simple first-law badge; no new forward force arrow.
shot_plan.controls: Inertia is a property, not an additional force.

cues.en: Relative to the slowing car, your body can move forward while restraints slow it too.
cues.zh: 相對於正在減速的車，身體可能向前移；同時，約束的力也讓身體減速。
cues.visual: Brief car-relative inset shows modest torso displacement against a fixed seat outline.

shot_plan.action: Brief car-relative inset shows modest torso displacement against a fixed seat outline.
shot_plan.controls: Explicitly label the changed frame; main ground-frame scene remains clear.

cues.en: The seat belt helps provide a backward force, reducing your body's forward speed.
cues.zh: 安全帶幫忙提供向後的力，降低身體向前移動的速度。
cues.visual: Show the belt's backward force on the torso, then shorten body velocity arrow.

shot_plan.action: Show the belt's backward force on the torso, then shorten body velocity arrow.
shot_plan.controls: Belt anchors remain attached to the car; do not claim it is the only contact force.

cues.en: So the forward lean does not require a mysterious new force pushing you forward.
cues.zh: 所以，往前傾並不需要一個神祕的新力量，把你往前推。
cues.visual: Remove the question mark at the passenger's front; keep only backward slowing-force arrow.

shot_plan.action: Remove the question mark at the passenger's front; keep only backward slowing-force arrow.
shot_plan.controls: No forward inertia force in the ground frame.

cues.en: The lean is relative motion. A backward force helps your body slow with the car.
cues.zh: 這個前傾是相對運動；向後的力，幫助身體跟著車子減速。
cues.visual: Car and passenger settle together with the belt visible.

shot_plan.action: Car and passenger settle together with the belt visible.
shot_plan.controls: Do not imply a universal measurable delay before any passenger force begins.

episodes.title_en: Why Does Water Climb a Paper Towel?
episodes.title_zh: 水為什麼會沿著紙巾往上爬？
episodes.question: How can water rise through paper without a pump?
episodes.description_en: Water wets cellulose fibers and spreads through tiny connected spaces. Capillary action can lift it against gravity, within limits.
episodes.description_zh: 水會潤濕纖維素纖維，並沿著連通的小空隙移動。這種毛細作用能讓水對抗重力上升，但並非沒有極限。

sources.title: Send Water Walking
sources.locator: Explanation of adhesion, cohesion and cellulose spaces, extracted lines 28–30.
sources.evidence: Paper towel has cellulose fibers and narrow spaces; attraction between water and fibers and between water molecules enables capillary movement.
sources.limits: Use the paper-wicking explanation; do not generalize its simplified tree-water statement to full tall-tree transport.

sources.title: Properties of Liquids
sources.locator: Paper towel Figure 10.19 and capillarity discussion, extracted lines 74–89 and 114–116.
sources.evidence: Adhesion to a porous material and cohesion within water explain wicking; in a simple vertical capillary, gravity limits rise.
sources.limits: An actual paper network is not a single uniform circular tube; do not apply its tube-height formula numerically to a towel.

sources.publisher: US Geological Survey Water Science School
sources.title: Capillary Action and Water
sources.locator: Initial successful text open, extracted lines 19–22, water movement in porous spaces and definitions.
sources.evidence: Capillary movement in porous spaces involves adhesion, cohesion and surface tension.
sources.limits: Initial text open succeeded; later requests timed out. Used as corroboration for the mechanism, not the sole evidence for the limiting height.

claims.text: Water can wick through the tiny spaces in paper because water is attracted to the cellulose fibers and to other water molecules.
limits: Use untreated absorbent paper towel. Waxed or hydrophobic paper may behave differently.

claims.text: Capillary action can raise water against gravity, but does not provide unlimited upward rise.
limits: The simple-channel inset illustrates gravity opposing rise; real paper has irregular connected pores, and finite strip length or evaporation may limit the observed wet front first.

invariants: The bottom of the paper stays in contact with reservoir water; the wet front remains connected to the water supply through wetted spaces.
Draw a fixed irregular fiber network with gaps between fibers. Water fills these spaces and wets surfaces; do not portray solid fibers as empty drinking straws.
Molecular inset uses equal-sized water symbols throughout; no water molecules grow and no new pores appear as a mechanism.
Show adhesion to fibers and cohesion between water symbols separately; avoid a literal rope-chain of molecules with rigid bonds.
Gravity still points downward. Do not animate an endlessly rising water column or a self-powered recirculating pump.
On-image words, including schematic and time-compression labels, are English only.
episodes.simplification: A qualitative connected-pore explanation. The ideal capillary inset illustrates the direction of forces, not an exact pore shape, measured rise height or drying model.

diagram_scale.paper: Paper strip x=420..650, y=540..1270 with bottom y=1270 immersed below a reservoir surface at y=1190.
diagram_scale.fiber_inset: Separate 520 by 400 px inset with 8 stationary curved cellulose-fiber strokes and visible connected gaps; 12 equal-radius water symbols used only as a local schematic.
diagram_scale.time: Wet front moves upward over compressed time; no claimed centimetres or seconds. A separate simplified channel shows gravity, not a paper-height prediction.

cues.en: Dip a paper towel into water. Why does the wet patch climb above the surface?
cues.zh: 把紙巾一端浸入水中。濕的部分為什麼會爬到水面上方？
cues.visual: Paper strip dips into a shallow cup; a wet tint creeps upward.

shot_plan.action: Paper strip dips into a shallow cup; a wet tint creeps upward.
shot_plan.controls: Paper remains in continuous contact with water; no hidden pump.

cues.en: Paper contains a tangled network of tiny fibers, with narrow connected spaces between them.
cues.zh: 紙裡有交錯的細小纖維，纖維之間留著狹窄、連通的空隙。
cues.visual: Magnify a labeled patch into a fixed network of fibers and inter-fiber spaces.

shot_plan.action: Magnify a labeled patch into a fixed network of fibers and inter-fiber spaces.
shot_plan.controls: Fibers are solid strokes, not hollow pipes.

cues.en: Water molecules are attracted to the cellulose fibers. That attraction is called adhesion.
cues.zh: 水分子會被纖維素纖維吸引；這種不同物質間的吸引，叫作附著力。
cues.visual: Equal-sized water symbols approach and wet a fiber surface.

shot_plan.action: Equal-sized water symbols approach and wet a fiber surface.
shot_plan.controls: No changing particle size or magical creation of water.

cues.en: Water molecules also attract one another. That attraction is called cohesion.
cues.zh: 水分子彼此之間也會吸引，這種吸引叫作內聚力。
cues.visual: Brief dotted attraction markers connect neighboring water symbols without rigid bonds.

shot_plan.action: Brief dotted attraction markers connect neighboring water symbols without rigid bonds.
shot_plan.controls: Attraction markers are symbolic, not a literal molecular crystal.

cues.en: Together, these effects let water spread through the narrow spaces, including upward against gravity.
cues.zh: 這些作用共同讓水沿著狹窄空隙移動，甚至能對抗重力向上爬。
cues.visual: Connected wet region advances through irregular gaps and along fiber surfaces.

shot_plan.action: Connected wet region advances through irregular gaps and along fiber surfaces.
shot_plan.controls: No detached flying liquid blobs or upward-flow arrows inside solid fibers.

cues.en: This movement through small spaces is capillary action. No hidden pump is needed.
cues.zh: 這種在小空隙裡移動的現象，就是毛細作用，不需要隱藏的幫浦。
cues.visual: Return to paper strip with a connecting zoom locator; wet front continues slowly.

shot_plan.action: Return to paper strip with a connecting zoom locator; wet front continues slowly.
shot_plan.controls: Do not imply the animation is recorded experimental footage.

cues.en: Gravity still pulls downward, so capillary action cannot lift water without limit.
cues.zh: 重力仍然向下拉，所以毛細作用不能讓水無限往上升。
cues.visual: Separate simplified vertical-channel inset shows a finite raised meniscus and downward weight.

shot_plan.action: Separate simplified vertical-channel inset shows a finite raised meniscus and downward weight.
shot_plan.controls: Do not assign this channel's equilibrium height to the actual paper strip.

cues.en: The towel soaks up water because its fibers and tiny spaces work together.
cues.zh: 紙巾能吸水，是纖維與細小空隙共同作用的結果。
cues.visual: Return to the familiar paper towel and highlight its connected wet region.

shot_plan.action: Return to the familiar paper towel and highlight its connected wet region.
shot_plan.controls: No universal claim about waxed paper or every liquid.

completion: All assigned episodes 13–20 drafted; ready for independent reader and factual review, not production approval.

research_access_limitations.result: Initial text open succeeded; later fetch/find requests timed out. Two other independent sources support the core claim.
Page description was opened and read; the full linked video was not watched.
